design_rationale: WORKLOG / DOSSIER — gift_cards_and_store_credit task 0 (round 1).  0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0, printed): {"task": 0, "key": "env_0031_online_fashion_retailer/gift_cards_and_store_credit/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. Tree = root + 1 prerequisite problem; both computations carry 5 factors. Task 1 draw (for headroom): prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [4, 5].  1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A Californian holder asks for her store credit to be paid in cash. The surface goal names no number and no prerequisite. The store credit is an instant Return Store Credit whose return has since been inspected (scarf graded C rejected; Chelsea boots graded B without their box, restocking 22.20 and missing-box 10.00 booked by the returns side), and the recovery the inspection makes owing has never been taken from the store credit. The cash-out policy says the cash-out amount is fixed only after the store credit's ledger carries the recovery entry for every inspected return whose instant credit was loaded onto it; a careful agent reads the ledger, sees the missing entry, finds from the recovery policy that its write books that entry, works out the recovery (five factors over returns, loyalty and Unlimited records), books it, and only then works out the cash-out amount (five factors over orders, returns, loyalty, claims and the instrument's own lock and refund history) on the lowered balance, handing the confirmation to the holder. Difficulty comes from discovering the prerequisite, reconciling the settlement record and the ledger, and getting ten ladders right; there is one tool per problem and no near-synonym tool.  2. SCOPE. Completed tasks: none. Claimed here: credit_ext_instant_credit_recovery (agent, claw_back_instrument_value_f010c427) and credit_ext_small_balance_cash_out (user, confirm_balance_cash_out_04a53640). Reserved headroom for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [4,5]): the lost/stolen replacement (credit_evt_lost_stolen: replacement value) and the holder-confirmed consolidation (credit_evt_cash_out consolidation clauses) — neither is touched by this task's policies or tools, and the recovery entry state stays singled out by this task's write only.  3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: credit_ext_small_balance_cash_out (trigger on_request; owner user). Prerequisite: credit_ext_instant_credit_recovery (trigger state_due; owner agent). Edge: kind value_input, gate balance_now (F('balance_usd') of the cash-out compute), form state, policy_source 'The cash-out amount is fixed only after the store credit's ledger carries the recovery entry owed for every return whose instant credit was loaded onto it and whose inspection results have posted.' Four-point test: (1) ordering connective 'only after', affirmative direction, joining this policy's own result (the cash-out amount) to what it waits on; contrapositive 'the cash-out amount is not fixed until ...' states the same scope; (2) XX is a record-visible state (a recovery entry on the store credit's ledger, read with find_credit_transactions; return inspection dates read with find_return_cases); (3) no tool, policy id or snake_case token; (4) strength 'only after', scope 'every return whose instant credit was loaded onto it and whose inspection results have posted', exactly the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a recovery entry for an inspected return: the recovery policy's rule says 'Return Store Credit issued before a return was inspected is clawed back, once the return's inspection results are posted, for the instant-credit recovery worked out below (reason failed_return_inspection), booked against the return's number', and its target tool is the only clawback writer. Derivation: sentence + ledger (no credit_clawed_back row; return a51d91c4 status inspected 2026-09-30) + recovery rule -> book the recovery first. Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.return_cases.a51d91c4.inspected_date = 2026-09-30 and the store credit's three ledger rows are credit_loaded / credit_redeemed / credit_refunded_to_instrument. Flip: the clawback write adds the recovery entry of 51.38, balance 60.31 -> 8.93. Topological order: recovery (step 11) then cash-out (step 18). Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping the recovery gives cash_out_usd 11.20 instead of 4.86. The persona names no return, inspection, recovery or adjustment; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block). The customer's own write is the cash-out: disposing of a balance is the holder's decision under the blueprint (lifecycle active -> closed by user), completed on the spot by the user tool.  4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Recovery write (subject credit_clawed_back): governing base policy credit_evt_clawback; gate one_clawback_per_source (dedup, system_record): no credit_clawed_back row exists for instrument 65c9ab44 with return a51d91c4 (ledger read) — satisfied; clawback_allowed is true for Return Store Credit; limited to the current balance (kept: the result is MN(balance, ...)). Overwrite declared: the base sentence 'clawed back for the value of the units the returns charter rejects at inspection' is replaced by the instant-credit recovery (rejected part plus fees as booked by the returns side, with the extended factors), aligning the credit charter with the returns charter's instant-credit reconciliation; all other clauses inherited. Cash-out write (subjects credit_closed_by_customer, credit_cashed_out): governing credit_evt_cash_out. Inherited: billing-state register keyed on customers.billing_state (CA: threshold 10.00, comparison below) — the balance after the recovery is 8.93 < 10.00, while the opening balance 60.31 is not (just-failing case 10.00, passing case 9.99); cash_out_eligible true for Return Store Credit; promotional value never cashed out (refined by the promotional exclusion); the instrument is active, not locked; mailed check within cash_out_processing_business_days. Overwrites declared: 'A cash-out closes the instrument for its whole balance; it is never partial.' (replaced: the cash-out pays the cash-out amount, the instrument closes only when nothing is left) and the confirmed-request sentence (replaced: the holder's own confirmation records the confirmed request in the same step) — this retires gate confirmed_request, so base_preconditions carries credit_evt_cash_out as policy_scope. No time gate applies to either write (temporal_feasibility []).  5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: Return Store Credit 65c9ab44 (source_reference = return a51d91c4, Store Credit Return of order e6e29071). Rows entering the recovery: the store credit's initial_issue load 1f8bd957 (316.10); settlement rows of return a51d91c4 only (line credits 4f545774 106.45 and 9b59f21e 160.77; fees f2654c55 -22.20 restocking and c2030f78 -10.00 missing box). Excluded: the February return 68b439d0 settlement rows (other return, refunded to card) and its instant credit (none). Rows entering the cash-out: the store credit's ledger (refund 2530dc7a +6.00 from the price adjustment on order e3be162c, which the store credit paid), the returned order's captures (537ad384 Rewards Note 40.00, 1eb084a6 card 276.10), the return's status, the loyalty membership, the claim events (none) and the store credit's locked_date. The Rewards Note a3ce6874 is closed and promotional — excluded from any disposal. The clawback writes the return's number as its correlation key.  6. FACTOR CARD (run on the handling-time worlds). Recovery (expected 51.38; whole baseline 60.31 = 48.88 + 22.20 + 10.00 = 81.08 limited to the 60.31 balance):  - restocking_cap_by_membership_length (parameter, loyalty cross-difficulty): enrolled 2020-11-03 = 71 whole months -> capped at 15.00 (booked 22.20). Baseline (uncapped) -> 54.08. Ladder: >=60 months 15.00 / 24-59 months 25.00 / otherwise uncapped.  - box_fee_share_by_unlimited_plan (parameter): Unlimited Standard Annual active, plan does not cover return labels -> 0.5 of 10.00 = 5.00. Baseline 1.0 -> 53.26. Near-miss: an Unlimited plan is held, but it is not one that covers labels (Express/Next-Day would give 0).  - late_inspection_absorption (parameter, returns cross-difficulty): received 2026-09-18, inspected 2026-09-30 = 12 calendar days -> half of the 20.00 fee part absorbed -> 10.00. Baseline (none) -> 58.88. Ladder: >14 days 1.0 / 8-14 days 0.5 / <=7 days 0.  - member_fee_treatment (method, multi-source, loyalty cross-difficulty): Gold AND 5 earning postings in the last 12 months (>=3) -> x0.75 rounded up to the cent = 7.50. Baseline (kept) -> 53.88. Near-miss: the June 2025 and December 2024 postings fall outside the 12-month window.  - first_recovery_allowance (parameter, returns cross-difficulty): inspected lines rejected/with fee in 24 months: 2, both on this return -> 0 on other returns -> 5.00. Baseline (none) -> 56.38. Near-miss: the February return's line is inspected but graded A accepted, so it does not count. Cash-out (expected 4.86; whole baseline 2.93 = 8.93 less the refund held under the standard 12-day period):  - promotional_tender_exclusion (method): returned order captured 40.00 of 316.10 by Rewards Note -> 2.93 x 40/316.10 = 0.37. Baseline (none) -> 5.23.  - unsettled_return_hold (parameter, returns cross-difficulty): return status inspected (not settled) -> 0.5 x 2.93 = 1.47. Baseline (none) -> 6.33.  - refund_availability_by_standing (parameter, loyalty cross-difficulty; tier and enrolment are one membership record, so the task's multi-source factor is member_fee_treatment): Gold AND enrolled 71 months (>=36) -> 7 days. Baseline 12 days -> refund held -> 0.36.  - delivery_claim_record_adjustment (parameter): no compensation in 24 months (her only claim, 85a15dc6, was denied) -> minus 1 day -> 6 days; the 6.00 refund of 2026-09-30 is exactly 6 days old and payable. Baseline (no adjustment) -> held -> 0.36. Near-miss: a delivery claim exists, but it carried no compensation.  - lifted_lock_reserve (parameter): most recent lock 2026-09-20, 16 days before -> 0.25 x 8.93 = 2.23. Baseline (none) -> 7.09. Per-factor sensitivity (gate-recomputed): recovery restocking_cap_by_membership_length -> 54.08; box_fee_share_by_unlimited_plan -> 53.26; late_inspection_absorption -> 58.88; member_fee_treatment -> 53.88; first_recovery_allowance -> 56.38; cash-out promotional_tender_exclusion -> 5.23; unsettled_return_hold -> 6.33; refund_availability_by_standing -> 0.36; delivery_claim_record_adjustment -> 0.36; lifted_lock_reserve -> 7.09. No factor reads a stamp: tiers rest on dates, counts and holdings (no 'discount applies' field exists).  7. WHY EACH ROW EXISTS. customers (identity, billing state CA); loyalty membership + 10 ledger rows (tier, enrolment, earning-postings window; the 4,000-point conversion behind the Rewards Note; points consistent: balance 810 = ledger sum; Silver multiplier 1.25 before the 2025-11-21 upgrade, Gold 1.5 after); Unlimited membership (box-fee share; also explains 0.00 shipping on Standard Ground orders); 7 orders (earning postings' parents; the returned order and the order the store credit paid); 7 order lines (returned units; the price-adjustment row behind the 6.00 refund; the February returned line); 5 order payments (captures by tender for the promotional share; the store-credit capture and refund matching the ledger); 2 instruments + 5 ledger rows (target store credit; the Rewards Note that paid part of the returned order); 2 returns + 8 lines + 7 settlements (the inspected store-credit return; the clean February return for the allowance); 1 delivery claim (claim record, denied). Removing the price-adjustment refund flips the availability ladders to decoration; removing the Rewards Note capture zeroes the promotional exclusion; removing the lock date zeroes the reserve; removing the February return's clean inspection leaves the allowance on its first tier but removes the near-miss. Automatic clauses checked: the store credit never expires; the Rewards Note closed on 2026-09-24 (30 days after its last transaction) before its 2026-09-28 expiry, so no forfeiture is owed; points pending periods have passed for everything except the September posting (no conversion owed: 810 < 2,000); the returns side's settlement of return a51d91c4 is still owed by the returns charter, which is exactly why the settlement hold applies, and it ignites nothing in this difficulty.  8. PERSONA DESIGN. Mireille Okafor, pediatric nurse on a lunch break, friendly and rushed; volunteers only the surface goal (cash instead of keeping the store credit), the coworker's California tip and a vague 'a little over sixty dollars'; email first; phone, date of birth, ZIP/state, check address and the September lock story only when asked; passive reactions to 'something has to be booked first' (go ahead), 'only part can be paid today' (accepts), 'nothing can be cashed out' (ends), and the hand-over (runs the tool with the agent's values); closes after the payout confirmation, raising no other topic. She volunteers no fact the opening world contradicts (she saw ~60 in the app; the balance is 60.31).  9. REACHABILITY WALK. Turn 1 request -> find_customers(email) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> instrument, ledger, returns, lines, settlements, loyalty, loyalty ledger, Unlimited reads expose every recovery input and the missing recovery entry -> agent explains a booking first; persona agrees -> unlock + clawback -> order, line, payment, claim reads expose the cash-out inputs -> agent explains the partial payout; persona accepts -> unlock_user + hand-over with instrument reference, CA and the amount -> the user tool runs, its receipt enters the transcript -> persona thanks and ends. All under frozen_time 2026-10-06 14:10:00 EDT; no wait, delivery, clearing or review is needed (the check is mailed after the call, which the cash-out write itself records as the payout).  10. CARELESS PATHS. Cashing out the opening 60.31 (prerequisite missed; also above the 10.00 threshold); clawing back only the rejected scarf (base sentence, superseded); taking the fees as booked (factors missed); applying the member treatment before the absorption (order pinned in the rule); holding the 6.00 refund under the standard 12 days; reserving 25% after taking off the exclusions instead of on the balance less held refunds; using banker's rounding on 1.465.  11. VERIFICATION (commands run): _author_t0_eval.py (temporary) evaluates both computes with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on the replayed worlds: recovery 51.38, cash-out 4.86, without the recovery 11.20; per-task gates check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding / check_cross_fire --task 0 all OK (outputs recorded in the final report of this round). Revision log: (a) symptom: member_fee_treatment baseline gave 53.25; root cause: '-int(-x)' floors positive values; change: true ceiling via int(v) + (v > int(v)); re-run: 53.26, gold unchanged. (b) symptom: replay reported 27 dangling foreign keys; root cause: empty references stored as ''; change: empty id references stored as null; re-run: REPLAY OK, closure 57/57.  11b. ROUND-2 (audit revision 1: task 0 PASS). Wording-only charter changes that bear on this task, compute and figures unchanged: the cash-out rule now states that the refund's date is day zero and the refunded value is payable on the day the count reaches the refund availability period (O-3: on 2026-10-06 the 2026-09-30 refund is exactly 6 days old against a 6-day period, so it is payable); promotional_tender_exclusion now declares returns as its cross-difficulty category (O-9; delivery_claim_record_adjustment stays null because this world holds no claim event rows for the gate to touch, O-T0-2). The multi-source label on refund_availability_by_standing was withdrawn (O-T0-3). Re-run: all gates OK, figures unchanged. 12. CLOSURE. policy -> tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: recovery -> claw_back_instrument_value_f010c427 -> clawback_usd at step 11 -> new credit_clawed_back row, balance lowered; cash-out -> confirm_balance_cash_out_04a53640 -> cash_out_usd at step 18 -> confirmed credit_requests row, credit_cashed_out row, balance lowered, instrument active. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies. Draft recomputation from the visible context alone (policy prose + tool schemas + read returns + persona lines) reaches the same order, objects and figures; the only judgement calls (calendar-day counting, the 'most recent refund' clock, the reserve base) are pinned verbatim in the rule.
user_scenario:
You are Mireille Okafor, a 39-year-old pediatric nurse in San Francisco who shops Marlowe & Finch a lot and is calling on her lunch break, friendly but a little rushed. You have some Marlowe & Finch store credit sitting on your account and you would rather have it as money than leave it there. A coworker told you that in California small gift-card and store-credit balances can be paid out in cash, so your request, in your own words, is: "I'd like the store credit on my account paid out to me in cash instead of keeping it, if that's possible." When you last looked in the app the store credit showed a little over sixty dollars, but you did not write the exact figure down and you are happy for the agent to look it up. You want it done today in this call, and you are fine with the agent sorting out whatever the account needs on their side; the only thing you expect to do yourself is approve the payout when they hand it to you.
You sign in with mireille.okafor@gmail.com and give that first if the agent asks how to find you. You only give other details when asked: your mobile is 4155550147 and your date of birth is 1987-06-21. If asked for your billing address details, your billing ZIP is 94117 and your state is California (CA). If the agent asks where a check should go, the address on your profile is right and you do not want it sent anywhere else. If the agent asks about the lock that was put on your store credit in September, you explain that you got a sign-in alert from your new phone, it was locked as a precaution, and it was unlocked once you confirmed it was you; nobody else has used your account. You do not know any reference numbers by heart.
You do not know Marlowe & Finch's rules and you do not suggest any steps. If the agent tells you something has to be booked on your account before the payout can be worked out, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead. If the agent explains that only part of the balance can be paid in cash today and the rest stays on your store credit for now, you are a bit disappointed but you accept it and still want the part they can pay. If the agent says nothing can be cashed out at all, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else. When the agent hands you the payout confirmation, you run it yourself with exactly the instrument reference, state and amount the agent gives you, and you read back what it returns if asked. Once the payout has been confirmed, you thank the agent and end the call; you do not raise any other topic.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.clawback_usd: 51.38. Rejected part 316.10 instant credit - 267.22 line credits = 48.88 (scarf, grade C); restocking part: booked 22.20 capped at 15.00 (membership enrolled 71 whole months, >= 60); box-fee part: booked 10.00 x 0.5 = 5.00 (Unlimited Standard Annual active, no return-label cover); fee part 20.00; late inspection: received 2026-09-18, inspected 2026-09-30 = 12 days -> half absorbed -> 10.00; member treatment: Gold with 5 earning postings in 12 months -> x0.75 rounded up -> 7.50; first-recovery allowance: no rejected or fee-charged line on the other return in 24 months -> 5.00 off; 48.88 + 7.50 - 5.00 = 51.38, below the 60.31 balance.

edges.condition: credit_transactions holds a credit_clawed_back row with clawback_reason failed_return_inspection and return_id equal to the store credit's source_reference for every such return whose return_cases.inspected_date is set.
edges.policy_source: The cash-out amount is fixed only after the store credit's ledger carries the recovery entry owed for every return whose instant credit was loaded onto it and whose inspection results have posted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The store-credit return's inspection posted on 2026-09-30 (scarf rejected, boots accepted with restocking and missing-box fees), but the store credit's ledger holds only its instant-credit load, the September spend and a price-adjustment refund: no recovery entry for that return exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The clawback write books a credit_clawed_back entry (failed_return_inspection, return a51d91c4-9aec-4809-8d3a-a812c1956cd9) of 51.38 and the store credit's balance becomes 8.93, which balance_now then reads.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the cash-out depends only on the recovery, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder. The order recovery-then-cash-out is pinned by the cash-out policy's prerequisite sentence, and the reverse order changes the terminal state (the cash-out would be worked out on the unrecovered balance).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the recovery write and replaying the cash-out on the unrecovered world gives cash_out_usd 11.20 instead of 4.86 (balance 60.31 instead of 8.93); the terminal state also lacks the clawback row, and the balance would not even be below California's 10.00 threshold.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario mentions only the store credit, a wish to have it paid in cash and the September security lock (asked-only). It never names the return, its inspection, a rejected or fee-charged unit, a recovery, a clawback or any adjustment; the customer's only reaction to a needed booking is passive ('say that is fine and ask them to go ahead') after the agent explains it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_balance_cash_out_04a53640 reads the instrument row only to copy the holder and compute the new balance, then creates the confirmed request and the cash-out entry unconditionally; it never checks whether a recovery is owed, the billing state or any balance threshold, so it remains callable and writes faithfully on the unrecovered store credit. claw_back_instrument_value_f010c427 likewise books whatever amount and reason it is given.
